act_title: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (CGST Act)
marginal_heading: Eligibility and Mandatory Conditions for Taking Input Tax Credit (ITC)
citation: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, Sec. 16
text: Every registered person is entitled to take credit of input tax charged on supply of goods/services used in business. Conditions: (a) possession of tax invoice or debit note; (b) details of invoice communicated in GSTR-2B; (c) goods or services received; (d) tax charged actually paid to Government by supplier; (e) recipient furnished return under Section 39. Recipient must pay supplier within 180 days from invoice date, failing which ITC must be reversed with interest.

act_title: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (CGST Act)
marginal_heading: Punishment for Certain Offences (Fake Invoicing, Bogus ITC, & Circular Trading)
citation: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, Sec. 132
text: Whoever commits or abets fake invoicing without supply, avails ITC using fake invoices, or fraudulently evades tax: (a) where amount exceeds Rs. 5 crore, punishable with imprisonment up to 5 years and fine (cognizable and non-bailable under Section 132(5)); (b) between Rs. 2 crore and Rs. 5 crore, imprisonment up to 3 years; (c) between Rs. 1 crore and Rs. 2 crore, imprisonment up to 1 year. Every repeat offence carries minimum 6 months imprisonment.

marginal_heading: Issue of Notice where Income has Escaped Assessment & Section 148A Inquiry
text: Before making reassessment under Section 147, Assessing Officer must serve notice under Section 148 requiring return. Post Finance Act 2021 and Supreme Court Ashish Agarwal ruling, AO must first conduct inquiry under Section 148A, provide information suggesting income escaping assessment, grant assessee 7 to 30 days to show cause, and pass speaking order under Section 148A(d) with prior approval of specified authority. Standard limitation is 3 years (extended to 10 years only if escaped income exceeds Rs. 50 lakh).

marginal_heading: Manner in Which Complaint Shall be Made to District Consumer Commission
text: A complaint in relation to any goods sold or service provided may be filed before the District Consumer Commission by: (a) consumer; (b) recognized consumer association; (c) Central Authority. District Commission has pecuniary jurisdiction up to Rs. 50 lakh (post 2021 rules). Complainant may file complaint electronically through e-Daakhil portal from place where complainant resides or works for gain. Admissibility decided within 21 days.

marginal_heading: Product Liability Action Against Manufacturer for Harm Caused by Defective Product
text: A product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action if: (a) product contains manufacturing defect; (b) product is defective in design; (c) there is deviation from manufacturing specifications; (d) product does not conform to express warranty; (e) product fails to contain adequate instructions for correct usage or warning of danger. Manufacturer is strictly liable even if he proves he was not negligent in making the product.
